newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea court to start appeal hearing on Chun, Roh.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea court to start appeal hearing on Chun, Roh.

text.p: South Korea's High Court will begin hearing appeals on Monday against sentences imposed on former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, court officials said.

Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in prison in August on charges of mutiny and treason stemming from a 1979 coup and the massacre of civilians demonstrating against martial law the following year in Kwangju.
The two men were also convicted of taking hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes.
Chun and Roh are appealing for their convictions to be quashed. State prosecutors are demanding that Roh's sentence be increased to life in jail, which is what they had demanded.
Fourteen former aides to Chun and Roh will also battle prosecutors trying to increase their sentences, which range from suspended jail terms to 10 years in prison.
The domestic Yonhap news agency said defence lawyers are expected to apply to the court to produce about 25 witnesses, while prosecutors would ask for 10 witnesses.
Hearings will be held twice each week initially, Yonhap said.
